title: The 10 Best Jobsite Radios
subtitle: Battery and plug-in jobsite radios and Bluetooth speakers for the garage, shop and jobsite, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A jobsite radio is built to take drops and dust and to run on the same batteries as your tools. We ranked 10 best-sellers from DEWALT, Milwaukee, Bosch, Makita, RYOBI and Sangean on rating, review volume and features (Bluetooth, AC power, charging your tool batteries and a weather rating). Start with the battery platform you already own.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Bluetooth Radio, 100 ft Range, Portable for Jobsites (DCR025)
products.best_for: DEWALT crews who want one box that plays music, charges batteries and powers chargers or lights.
products.verdict: A bigger DEWALT radio that doubles as a charger and power strip: plugged in, it charges 20V MAX and FLEXVOLT batteries at 3 amps and gives you two extra AC outlets.
pros: Charges DEWALT batteries at 3 A on AC

specs.extras: Charges 20V/60V batteries at 3 A, 2 AC outlets, 20 W per channel

products.name: DEWALT 12V/20V MAX Portable Bluetooth Radio, Cordless, 100 ft Range, 3.5" Subwoofers (DCR028B)
products.best_for: DEWALT owners who want a tough, good-sounding radio for the shop or jobsite.
products.verdict: The best seller and the most-reviewed radio here. It runs on any DEWALT 12V, 20V MAX or FLEXVOLT battery or the included AC cord, with dual 3.5-inch woofers, Bluetooth and a roll cage.
pros: Roll cage and USB charging port

specs.power: DEWALT 12V, 20V MAX, FLEXVOLT or AC cord
specs.extras: Roll cage, USB charging port, aux input

products.name: Milwaukee 2951-20 M12 Lithium-Ion Cordless Radio + Charger (Tool Only)
products.best_for: M12 owners who want a small, hangable radio for a van, garage or attic.
products.verdict: A small M12 radio and charger that's rated IP54 against water and dust. The listing claims up to 10 hours on an M12 2.0Ah battery, and it hangs from a keyhole or its hollow handle.
pros: About 10 hours on an M12 2.0Ah pack
cons: No AC cord listed, just a 12V DC port

specs.extras: IP54, about 10 hr on an M12 2.0Ah pack, keyhole hanger

products.name: Milwaukee M18 PACKOUT Radio + Charger (2950-20)
products.best_for: Milwaukee crews already using PACKOUT boxes.
products.verdict: Milwaukee's big radio-and-charger that locks into the PACKOUT storage system. The listing is short, but it plays Bluetooth and AM/FM, charges M18 batteries and lists a waterproof rating.

products.name: Sangean LB-100 Worksite AM/FM Utility Radio, Tough, Water Resistant
products.best_for: Anyone who just wants reliable AM/FM in a garage or shop, on any tool brand.
products.verdict: A plain, rugged AM/FM radio that plugs into the wall. It's rain, dust and shock resistant with a 5-inch speaker and 10 presets, but no Bluetooth and no battery option on this listing.
pros: Works with no tool batteries at all

products.name: Makita XRM06B 18V LXT Lithium-Ion Cordless Bluetooth Job Site Radio
products.best_for: Makita owners who want long runtime from batteries they already have.
products.verdict: A Makita radio that runs on almost any Makita battery from 7.2V to 18V LXT. The listing claims up to 35 hours on an 18V 5.0Ah pack, with dust- and water-resistant construction.
pros: Up to 35 hours on a 5.0Ah battery

specs.extras: Up to 35 hr on a 5.0Ah pack, water resistant

products.name: BOSCH GPB18V-5CN 18V Jobsite Radio with Bluetooth 5.0 and Power Station
products.best_for: Bosch 18V users who want a radio that also powers lights and chargers.
products.verdict: A Bosch radio and power station with four 120V outlets, a 2.1-amp USB port and four-way speakers with a subwoofer that project in all directions.

products.name: BOSCH GPB18V-2CN 18V Cordless Jobsite Radio with Bluetooth 5.0 (Battery Not Included)
products.best_for: Bosch 18V owners who want a compact, weather-rated radio.
products.verdict: Bosch's smaller 18V radio, rated IP54, with Bluetooth 5.0, AM/FM and the option to pair two units for wider stereo sound.

specs.extras: IP54, pairs with a second unit for stereo

products.name: Milwaukee M18 Bluetooth Jobsite Radio, Bare Tool
products.best_for: Milwaukee M18 owners who want a compact jobsite speaker and radio.
products.verdict: Milwaukee's current M18 radio, with dual 3.5-inch woofers, dual tweeters and Bluetooth 5.0 with up to 120 ft of range. It runs on any M18 battery or the included AC adapter.

products.name: RYOBI 18V ONE+ Compact Bluetooth Radio
products.best_for: RYOBI owners who want music in the garage for little money.
products.verdict: The cheapest radio here by far: a compact RYOBI ONE+ unit with a 15-watt speaker, FM radio, USB charging and the longest Bluetooth range listed here.

avoid.name: RIDGID 18V Hybrid JOBSITE Radio with Bluetooth Technology Tool ONLY R84089B
avoid.flag: Listing's only bullet describes lawn-mower parts
avoid.verdict: The radio may be fine, but this listing can't tell you anything about it: its only bullet is about Stens lawn and landscape replacement parts.
reasons: The single product bullet reads 'Stens replacement parts have become a favorite among lawn and landscape professionals', which has nothing to do with a radio.
With no description, you can't confirm the tuner, Bluetooth range, runtime or what power cord comes in the box before buying.
The same 'Stens' bullet appears on other RIDGID and RYOBI listings we've reviewed, a sign the listing data was copied in wholesale rather than written for this product.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a radio that matches my tool batteries?
buyers_guide.a: If you own cordless tools, yes. A radio on the same platform runs all day on packs you already charge, and most also take an AC cord for the shop. If you don't own tool batteries, a plug-in radio like the Sangean LB-100 is simpler.
Some radios, like the DEWALT DCR025 and Milwaukee's PACKOUT radio, charge your tool battery while plugged into the wall. That saves carrying a separate charger to the job.
Not much on a jobsite. 100 feet is plenty if your phone is in your pocket. Range drops through walls and around metal.
IP54 means protected against dust and splashing water from any direction. It's fine for light rain, not for leaving out in a storm.

buyers_guide.q: How long will it run on a battery?
buyers_guide.a: Small radios run 10 hours or more on a 2.0Ah pack. Makita claims up to 35 hours on a 5.0Ah pack for the XRM06B. Volume and bass settings make a big difference.
